To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ATP5EP1 gene, which encodes the epsilon subunit, has been identified on human chromosome 20 and that a pseudogene of the epsilon subunit gene is present on chromosome 4.

the human ATP5 gene is mapped to chromosome 20q, that the epsilon subunit is expressed in all 16 tissues tested, that a pseudogene is identified on chromosome 4, and that a conserved motif is defined on the basis ATP synthase epsilon sequences from ten different organisms, which we believe will be of value in the study of this gene.

a new conserved motif, termed the ATPSE motif, was identified on the basis that it is present in the epsilon subunit from 10 different organisms, and that the human ATP5 gene is mapped on chromosome 20q, and a pseudogene, ATP5EP1 is localized on chromosome 4q.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning, mapping and characterization of the human ATP synthase epsilon gene, and the identification of a new conserved motif and a pseudogene.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ATP5A1-ATP5E gene cluster on human chromosome 20 contains at least three functional genes, ATP5A1, ATP5E and a third ATP5E-like gene (ATP5EL), and two pseudogenes, ATP5EP1 and ATP5EP2.
there are at least four ATP5E sequences (three genes and one pseudogene) in the human genome, and that the ATP5EP1 pseudogene is the most likely to have arisen from gene duplication.

the human ATP synthase epsilon gene is a single gene on human chromosome 20, and the ATP5E pseudogene on chromosome 4 is the only one in the human genome, with a total of three homologous sequences of the epsilon gene in the human genome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ATP5A, ATP5B, ATP5E and the ATP synthase inhibitor factor 1 (ATP5IF1) genes are all located on human chromosome 20, whereas the ATP5F gene is on chromosome 4.
there are at least two genes (ATP5E and ATPESP1) and three pseudogenes of ATP5E in the human genome.
the ATP5 gene family in human comprises four genes, ATP5A1, ATP5E (including ATP5EP1), ATP5F1 and ATP5G1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ATP5EP1 sequence is the only one in the human genome which can be considered a true pseudogene, whereas all others are likely to be functional genes.
the epsilon subunit, a key component of ATP synthase, is a highly conserved molecule among different species and is essential to the function of the ATP synthase complex in eukaryotic cells.
the ATP5A, ATP5B, ATP5C, ATP5D, ATP5E and possibly ATP5G genes are all present on human chromosome 20, whereas there is no evidence for ATP5F or ATP5H genes in the human genome.
